capacity_gross_kwh.notes: 35.5 kWh prismatic lithium ion (Mazda figure, relayed).

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Green Cars Compare: "The 35.5 kWh battery (30 kWh usable)" (spec site, not attributed to Mazda).
ArenaEV (European car): 31 kWh usable. Sources disagree by 1 kWh.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: "400 V architecture" per Green Cars Compare; ArenaEV lists 355 V (class 400v).

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: No Mazda page found describing a battery-warming or charge-preconditioning feature; the InsideEVs/Fastned DC tests show a plain curve with no preconditioning mentioned. Compared 2022-2024: no change found.

chemistry.notes: Estimated: ADAC manufacturer-data table for the European MX-30 (09/20-04/22, 35.5 kWh gross) lists Nickel-Mangan-Cobalt; same 35.5 kWh pack in the 2022-2024 North American cars (2020-2022 ADAC page compared with the 2022-2024 NA cars).

ac_max_kw.notes: "6.6 kW AC (1 phase, 230V, 29A)" (Wikipedia; Green Cars Compare also 6.6 kW).

dc_max_kw.notes: Fastned: MX-30 2020-2023 max charge speed 40 kW; Wikipedia: 40 kW; InsideEVs measured about 37 kW. Fastned lists 55 kW for the 2023+ European car; North American 2023-2024 cars not confirmed either way. Conflict: the Mazda USA 2021 release reportedly says DC 50 kW (about 36 min to 80%) but I could not find that page; the Green Cars Compare generic line that the USA version has no DC fast charging is contradicted by the car having a CCS1 DC inlet.
